request.deadline: 12 months, with stated milestones at weeks 6, 12, 13, 16, 18, 24, 26, 39, and 52
deliverables: dOSPO operational team and program management systems
two advisory councils with published feedback before disbursements
501(c)(3) dOSPO legal entity and published governance documents
quarterly public reports with Mill Law Firm financial review
dependency audit with SBOMs, centrality scores, bus-factor assessments, and coverage gap analysis
maintenance fund retainers for high-risk Cardano open source infrastructure
request.recipient: Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting as administrator at treasury withdrawal, with intended operational transition to a dOSPO legal entity subject to governance.
request.what: Establish a one-year independent Cardano dOSPO and Open Maintenance Framework program to manage open source sustainability funds, create advisory councils, form a 501(c)(3) public charity, fund maintenance retainers and related programs, and publish quarterly reports.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,094,000 ADA over 12 months for a dOSPO and OMF program.
Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting is designated as the sole Article II.7.5 administrator from treasury withdrawal through the 12-month period.
Mill Law Firm is designated as independent financial auditor on a quarterly cadence through Month 12.
The proposal states that no WP2-WP5 disbursement will be made before advisory council feedback is published, while final allocation authority remains with the administrator.
The program will form two advisory councils by Week 6 and a 501(c)(3) dOSPO legal entity by Week 24, subject to legal processes and governance.
WP2 allocates 2,000,000 ADA to maintenance retainers for Cardano open source infrastructure selected using dependency centrality, bus-factor analysis, SBOMs, and a published rubric.
The proposal asserts that Cardano lacks an operational layer to translate governance decisions into sustained accountable maintenance programs.
The proposer claims prior experience as Senior Manager of Open Source Governance and Head of OSPO at Intersect, where he built open source governance functions and shaped the Paid Open Source Model.
The proposal claims the dOSPO and OMF whitepapers were developed with experts from several named organizations and communities.

The proposal targets funding 15 or more high-centrality projects by Month 12, funding 40% of top-50 dependencies, maintaining 100% quarterly reporting, and reaching defined contributor, attrition, and response-time KPIs.

summary: The document describes a 4,094,000 ADA, one-year open source sustainability program with a named administrator, named auditor, advisory councils, legal-entity formation, maintenance funding, dependency analysis, public reporting, and KPI targets, but several key need and track-record claims are asserted or externally checkable rather than evidenced inside the document.
